title: Source register and bounded evidence
evidence_policy: Primary public project/spec/documentation sources plus the exact authorized case files. Each Sxx.md contains a short excerpt or precise locator, a version/identity statement, a retrieval window, limits, and an interpretation. Hashes identify local evidence note bytes; S00 records original case-file SHA-256 values. Live documentation URLs can move, so version uncertainty is explicit.

sources.title: SQLite transaction control
sources.version: SQLite official living documentation; page last updated 2026-02-18; no engine release pin
sources.method: web.run direct open of official documentation
sources.identity: Exact official URL; live doc snapshot captured as a bounded locator/excerpt
sources.excerpt: SQLite supports multiple simultaneous read transactions ... but only one simultaneous write transaction.
sources.interpretation: A local app can atomically commit an inspection change, outbox row, and pull cursor; a single-writer client must handle SQLITE_BUSY.
sources.limitations: Docs do not establish the app’s power-loss behavior, encryption, OS filesystem durability, or a particular SQLite library version.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 INSERT / ON CONFLICT
sources.version: PostgreSQL 17 documentation (current patch not pinned by docs URL)
sources.method: web.run direct open of official documentation
sources.excerpt: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE guarantees an atomic INSERT or UPDATE outcome ... even under high concurrency.
sources.interpretation: A unique tenant/event key can make duplicate event receipt safe at the database boundary.
sources.limitations: The app still must compare payload hashes and reject reuse of an event ID with different bytes; SQL alone does not implement the sync protocol.

sources.title: RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics
sources.version: RFC 9110 (June 2022)
sources.method: web.run direct open of RFC Editor text
sources.identity: Stable RFC number and published text
sources.excerpt: PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent.
sources.interpretation: PUT to a client-chosen stable event URI is a sound retry shape if repeated same-content writes have the same intended effect.
sources.limitations: The server’s semantics must enforce this; RFC method properties do not provide event deduplication or exactly-once delivery.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB 3.5 replication and conflict model
sources.version: Apache CouchDB documentation family 3.5; stable URL is rolling, no patch-specific source identity
sources.method: web.run direct open; official docs page title identifies 3.5
sources.locator: §2.3.1–2.3.4, revision tree, GET ?conflicts=true, compaction, resolver steps
sources.excerpt: The deterministically-chosen winner is the only revision fed into your map function.
sources.interpretation: CouchDB preserves conflicting leaf revisions, but default reads/views can conceal them; app resolver and conflict queue remain necessary.
sources.limitations: This is 3.5 documentation, not proof of patch-specific behavior in every deployment.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB 3.5 replication protocol
sources.version: Apache CouchDB documentation family 3.5; stable URL is rolling, no patch-specific source identity
sources.method: web.run direct open; official docs page title identifies 3.5
sources.excerpt: The Replicator SHOULD expect to be working within an unstable environment with delays, losses and other bad surprises.
sources.interpretation: Existing replication systems explicitly model retries and checkpoints; a fresh system needs equivalent failure tests.
sources.limitations: Protocol recommendations are not an implementation guarantee for this proposed API.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB 3.5 attachment API
sources.version: Apache CouchDB documentation family 3.5; stable URL is rolling
sources.method: web.run direct open
sources.excerpt: Range requests are available for all attachments inside CouchDB.
sources.interpretation: CouchDB can serve attachment byte ranges; this says nothing about resumable upload or photo identity in the proposed service.
sources.limitations: Not used as evidence that partial uploads are idempotent.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB 3.5 database security API
sources.version: Apache CouchDB documentation family 3.5; stable URL is rolling
sources.method: web.run direct open
sources.excerpt: Members can read all types of documents from the DB.
sources.interpretation: Database membership is not equivalent to per-asset read authorization; use a protected application API or a carefully partitioned design.
sources.limitations: CouchDB has extensible update validation; this source is specifically about database-level member/admin rights.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB 3.5 purge semantics
sources.version: Apache CouchDB documentation family 3.5; stable URL is rolling
sources.method: web.run direct open
sources.excerpt: Purge operations are not replicated to other external databases.
sources.interpretation: Logical delete tombstones and irreversible physical purge are different operations; deleting a row is not a safe retention protocol.
sources.limitations: Applies to CouchDB purge behavior, not the proposed event service.

sources.title: PouchDB issue #8525

sources.method: web.run direct open of Apache PouchDB GitHub issue

sources.interpretation: Compaction policy can affect foreground writes and must be included in offline-device soak tests.

sources.excerpt: Public native app clients MUST implement the Proof Key for Code Exchange extension.
